headline: Rewindable proofs give weak verifiers a new route to check robust computations
summary: A new paper introduces rewindable interactive proofs, in which a verifier can restore an AI prover to a saved interaction state and ask new questions from there. For robust oracle computations, the authors prove a relativizing protocol with a succinct verifier and a linear-time honest prover, without assuming that a prover is truthful or using cryptography. The paper reports a proof-of-concept MNIST experiment and a BLAKE3 comparison, while explicitly saying the experiments are not a realistic scalable-oversight benchmark. A linked public repository supplies code, result ledgers and scripts, but clarifies that timed runs do not restore a machine state; general preprocessing and real model-state restoration costs remain unresolved, so deployed oversight benefits are not established.
